latest_apis.rationale: The data-loading half of the router (routeLoader$, DocumentHead with resolveValue, status(404), adapters, build scripts) is genuinely on the newest stable release and matches current docs, but the navigation half is skipped entirely: no <Link>, so every internal link is an MPA full-page reload with no prefetching, and the home page hand-rolls the URL/history handling that useNavigate() (already used one page over) exists for. Sources: qwik.dev/docs/routing and /docs/advanced/routing (Dynamic 404 Page pattern), learn-qwik.com tutorial ('Currently the links use <a> elements… a full page refresh on each navigation'), and the runtime in app/dist/build/q-j0Grn1fb.js.

churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, env configuration and build configuration are well isolated and the starter boilerplate is current enough that a framework upgrade touches few files. The offsetting liability is the home page's ~60 lines of duplicated router responsibility that only work because of undocumented Qwik City internals, plus copy-pasted 404 handling across five routes and unchecked `any` payloads at the API boundary.

findings.issue: No <Link> from @builder.io/qwik-city is used anywhere; every internal link is a plain <a>, and the shipped Qwik City runtime only intercepts same-page anchors, so all navigation is a full page reload with no SPA transitions, no route-data prefetching and no bundle preloading — Qwik's headline benefit is left off the table.
findings.suggestion: Replace internal <a href> with <Link> (it accepts the same attributes and adds prefetch, replaceState and scroll options); the layout nav, Pokémon cards and pagination links all qualify.

findings.issue: Filter/pagination URL state is managed by raw window.history.pushState/replaceState plus a useVisibleTask$ popstate listener that reads useLocation().url — this only works because Qwik City monkey-patches history.pushState to carry its internal _qCityScroll state and falls back to location.reload() on popstate when no a[q:link] exists, i.e. it is coupled to framework internals and is inconsistent with app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:125-128 which uses useNavigate().
findings.suggestion: Drive query state through useNavigate() (or <Link replaceState>) and read it reactively from useLocation().url.searchParams; that deletes buildHomeUrl's callers' manual history calls, the popstate listener and the four mirrored useSignals.

findings.issue: eslint, @eslint/js, eslint-plugin-qwik, globals and typescript-eslint are installed but app/ contains no eslint.config.js, so `npm run lint` fails and the framework's own Qwik-specific rules (which catch resumability and event-handler mistakes across upgrades) never run.
findings.suggestion: Add the starter's eslint.config.js (it ships with create-qwik@1.20.3 and wires eslint-plugin-qwik + typescript-eslint), or remove the five packages and the lint scripts.

findings.issue: The API boundary is typed only on the way out: payloads are `any` throughout (englishName(names: any[]), TypeInfo.detail: any, evolutionTree(node: any)) and render sites add `(type: any)`/`(stat: any)`/`(move: any)` annotations that discard the loader's inferred types, so upstream field renames surface as silent undefined at runtime rather than a type error.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the PokeAPI payloads next to the view models in lib/api.ts and drop the explicit `any` annotations in the route files so the loader models flow through.

findings.issue: "undici": "*" is never imported (the code uses global fetch), uses a floating range, and the lockfile resolves undici 8.12.3 which requires Node >=22.19.0 while the package's engines field still allows Node 18/20 — an install-time hazard inherited from the starter template.
findings.suggestion: Remove the undici devDependency (and while there, either drop the stale 'sharp' engines-annotation or align engines with the Node version you actually run).

findings.issue: typescript-plugin-css-modules is pinned to "latest" (unreproducible) but the app has no CSS modules; tsconfig.json:21 still carries the starter's instruction to delete it in that case.
findings.suggestion: Remove the plugin from devDependencies and the "plugins" entry from tsconfig.json, per the starter's own comment.

findings.issue: The not-found flow (status(404) in a loader, {notFound:true} sentinel, NotFound render, head ternary) is copy-pasted across five route files, and the catch-all route needs a routeLoader that does nothing but call status(404).
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared helper (e.g. a `notFoundOr(data)` wrapper plus one shared head builder) and consider the documented src/routes/404.tsx convention for unmatched paths, which the router statically emits as 404.html instead of SSR-ing every 404.

findings.issue: fetchJson has no AbortController or timeout, and the in-flight promise is cached permanently, so one hung API request stalls that route for the lifetime of the process with no way to recover.
findings.suggestion: Wrap fetches in AbortSignal.timeout(...) (or a signal keyed off the request) and evict the cache entry on abort as well as on error.

findings.issue: typescript is pinned to 5.4.5 (≈2 years old) and @types/node to 20.19.0 while the declared runtime is Node 24, so newer language/platform types are invisible to build.types.
findings.suggestion: Bump typescript to the current 5.x and @types/node to the 24.x line (both are drop-in here; typescript-eslint 8.38 already supports them).

findings.issue: The app ships no tests of its own (the acceptance suite is external), and the pure helpers most likely to drift — humanize/dexNumber/displayNumber and compareRows/MoveTable sorting — are trivially unit-testable but unguarded.
findings.suggestion: Add a minimal vitest suite for format.ts and the MoveTable sort comparator so future refactorings and framework upgrades don't regress the display rules.

summary: This is a current-release Qwik City app: pinned to the latest stable (1.20.3), with starter files that match a fresh `create-qik` generation byte-for-byte and routeLoader$-based data loading that follows today's docs, backed by a clean single-module data layer and an empty production dependency graph. The two things that will age badly are the navigation and the lint setup: no <Link> anywhere means every internal click is a full page reload, the home page reimplements ~60 lines of router responsibility that only works because of undocumented Qwik City internals, and the installed eslint stack has no config file so the framework's own lint rules never run. Fix those three and this becomes an easy app to own.
